headline: High-risk filesystem and network interaction: Mentat can modify shared files while Rasa can expose conversation data to external channels, creating leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat writes and reads the filesystem and shares state via filesystem across instances, so if Rasa outputs are copied into shared files or logs, attacker-controlled text can be reinterpreted as instructions. Rasa’s allowlisted networked chat channels make such content plausible, but no direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Rasa messages are copied into files that Mentat reads as task context
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or transcript file
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Strip instructions from any text copied from Rasa before Mentat reads it
Use a read-only handoff file for Rasa outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat can read and write selected files and sends context to a configured model provider; Rasa handles text and voice and can relay conversation content through messaging APIs. If they share a workspace or transcript store, sensitive text can flow from one agent into the other and onward. The exact shared storage is not documented, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same transcript or workspace directory
IF conversation text includes secrets or personal data
mitigations: Keep Rasa transcripts out of Mentat’s workspace
Disable automatic export of conversation logs
Redact secrets before any file handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has filesystem write and git-state modification, while Rasa can operate as a multi-channel bot with allowlisted network egress. Their capabilities overlap on mutable project artifacts if they share a directory or deployment repo, creating race conditions and conflicting edits. Because Rasa’s write surface is not explicit, uncertainty pushes this to medium instead of low.
conditions: IF Rasa writes configuration or logs into the same repository Mentat edits
IF both agents modify the same files without locking
mitigations: Assign separate repos or directories
Freeze git writes while Rasa is active
Use file locks on shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and Rasa can surface conversational text through chat channels; if Rasa consumes Mentat’s output as authoritative, a mistaken edit plan can cascade into user-facing responses or operational actions. No verification step is documented between them, but direct action authority is also not shown, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Rasa uses Mentat-generated text as a source of truth
IF downstream responses are sent without human review
mitigations: Require human review of Mentat diffs before Rasa uses them
Add a verification step that checks Mentat output against source files
Limit Rasa to summarizing, not executing, Mentat output
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware validation

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat touches source code and model-provider API keys, while Rasa handles text and voice across messaging platforms. The profiles do not show a residency or regulated-data mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is plausible if sensitive customer text is routed into Mentat’s external model provider. The other agent is not cited for residency because none is documented.
conditions: IF customer-support text contains regulated personal data
IF that text is forwarded from Rasa into Mentat’s model-provider calls
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated text to Mentat
Redact PII before handoff
Review vendor DPAs for the model provider
requires-engineering: segregate regulated workloads
